sections.title: What Are Foundations?
sections.body:
> **"You can't build a skyscraper without a solid foundation"**

The absolute bedrock concepts every agentic AI engineer must master. Without these, everything built on top is shaky. These are NOT basic — they are the precise mechanics of how LLMs think, communicate, and act.

sections.title: 1.1 — LLM Fundamentals
sections.body:
```
┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│                    HOW AN LLM WORKS                             │
└─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘

  INPUT TEXT                    OUTPUT TEXT
  ──────────                    ───────────
  "What is                      "Paris is the
   the capital                   capital of
   of France?"                   France."
       │                              ▲
       ▼                              │
  ┌────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
  │                   TRANSFORMER ENGINE                       │
  │                                                            │
  │  Tokenize → Embed → Self-Attention → FFN → Predict Next    │
  │                                                            │
  │  "What" "is" "the" "capital" "of" "France" "?"            │
  │    ↓      ↓    ↓       ↓       ↓     ↓      ↓             │
  │  [tok1] [tok2] [tok3] [tok4] [tok5] [tok6] [tok7]         │
  │                         ↓                                  │
  │              Attention: which tokens                        │
  │              are related to each other?                     │
  │              "capital" ←→ "France" (high weight)           │
  │                         ↓                                  │
  │              Output: "Paris" (highest probability)          │
  └────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘

  KEY PARAMETERS THAT MATTER FOR AGENTS:
  ┌─────────────────┬────────────────────────────────────────┐
  │  Temperature    │  0.0 = deterministic (tools/facts)     │
  │                 │  0.7 = creative (writing)              │
  │                 │  1.0+ = very random (brainstorming)    │
  ├─────────────────┼────────────────────────────────────────┤
  │  Max Tokens     │  Limits output length                  │
  │                 │  Set too low → truncated responses     │
  ├─────────────────┼────────────────────────────────────────┤
  │  Top-P          │  Nucleus sampling                      │
  │                 │  0.9 = sample from top 90% probability │
  ├─────────────────┼────────────────────────────────────────┤
  │  Context Window │  GPT-4o: 128K tokens                   │
  │                 │  Claude 3.5: 200K tokens               │
  │                 │  Gemini 1.5: 1M tokens                 │
  └─────────────────┴────────────────────────────────────────┘
```

sections.title: 1.2 — Tokenization
sections.body:
```
┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│                      TOKENIZATION                               │
│  "LLMs don't see words — they see TOKENS"                      │
└─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘

  WHAT IS A TOKEN?
  A chunk of text — could be a word, part of a word, or punctuation.

  "Hello, world!" → ["Hello", ",", " world", "!"] → 4 tokens

  MORE EXAMPLES:
  ┌────────────────────────────────┬───────────────┬──────────┐
  │  Text                          │  Tokens       │  Count   │
  ├────────────────────────────────┼───────────────┼──────────┤
  │  "cat"                         │  ["cat"]      │  1       │
  │  "cats"                        │  ["cats"]     │  1       │
  │  "unbelievable"                │  ["un","bel", │  4       │
  │                                │  "iev","able"]│          │
  │  "ChatGPT"                     │  ["Chat","GPT"]│  2      │
  │  "I love Python"               │  ["I"," love",│  3       │
  │                                │   " Python"]  │          │
  └────────────────────────────────┴───────────────┴──────────┘

  TOKEN COSTS (GPT-4o, April 2025):
  ┌──────────────────┬──────────────────┬──────────────────────┐
  │  Type            │  Price           │  1M tokens cost      │
  ├──────────────────┼──────────────────┼──────────────────────┤
  │  Input tokens    │  $5.00/1M        │  $5.00               │
  │  Output tokens   │  $15.00/1M       │  $15.00              │
  │  Cached input    │  $2.50/1M        │  $2.50               │
  └──────────────────┴──────────────────┴──────────────────────┘

  RULE OF THUMB:
  1 token ≈ 4 characters ≈ 0.75 words
  1 page of text ≈ 500-750 tokens
  1000-word essay ≈ 1,300 tokens

  WHY THIS MATTERS FOR AGENTS:
  • Every tool description uses tokens
  • Every memory retrieved uses tokens
  • Every message in history uses tokens
  • More tokens = more cost + higher latency
```

sections.title: 1.5 — Embeddings & Similarity Search
sections.body:
```
┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│                 EMBEDDINGS & VECTOR SEARCH                      │
│  "Turning text into numbers that capture meaning"               │
└─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘

  WHAT IS AN EMBEDDING?
  A list of numbers (vector) that represents the MEANING of text.

  "King"   → [0.2, 0.8, -0.1, 0.5, ...]  (1536 numbers)
  "Queen"  → [0.2, 0.7, -0.1, 0.5, ...]  (very similar!)
  "Apple"  → [0.9, 0.1,  0.8, 0.2, ...]  (very different)

  SEMANTIC SIMILARITY:
  ┌──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
  │  Query: "What is RAG?"                                       │
  │  Vector: [0.3, 0.7, 0.2, ...]                                │
  │                                                              │
  │  Database:                                                   │
  │  Doc A: "RAG retrieves documents for LLMs"  sim=0.95 ← BEST │
  │  Doc B: "Vector databases store embeddings" sim=0.72         │
  │  Doc C: "Python is a programming language"  sim=0.15         │
  └──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘

  COSINE SIMILARITY FORMULA:
  similarity = (A · B) / (||A|| × ||B||)
  Range: -1 (opposite) to 1 (identical)
  > 0.85 = very similar
  > 0.70 = related
  < 0.50 = unrelated
```

sections.title: Layer 1 Code Examples
sections.body:
**What this code covers**

- Layer 1: Function Calling + Structured Output + Embeddings Complete foundational examples.
- 1. BASIC FUNCTION CALLING
- No tool call → final answer
- Execute each tool call
- 2. STRUCTURED OUTPUT (JSON MODE)
- 3. EMBEDDINGS & SIMILARITY SEARCH

**Defines:** `demo_function_calling()`, `demo_structured_output()`, `demo_embeddings()`

```python name=layer1_foundations/function_calling.py
"""
Layer 1: Function Calling + Structured Output + Embeddings
Complete foundational examples.
"""
import os
import json
import math
import numpy as np
from openai  import AzureOpenAI
from dotenv  import load_dotenv

load_dotenv()

client = AzureOpenAI(
    azure_endpoint = os.getenv("AZURE_OPENAI_ENDPOINT"),
    api_key        = os.getenv("AZURE_OPENAI_API_KEY"),
    api_version    = os.getenv("AZURE_OPENAI_API_VERSION"),
)
MODEL      = os.getenv("AZURE_OPENAI_DEPLOYMENT")
EMBED_MODEL= os.getenv("AZURE_OPENAI_EMBEDDING_DEPLOYMENT","text-embedding-ada-002")

# ════════════════════════════════════════════════════
# 1. BASIC FUNCTION CALLING
# ════════════════════════════════════════════════════

def demo_function_calling():
    print("\n" + "="*55)
    print("🔧 1. FUNCTION CALLING DEMO")
    print("="*55)

    # Define tools
    tools = [
        {
            "type": "function",
            "function": {
                "name": "calculator",
                "description": "Evaluate any mathematical expression",
                "parameters": {
                    "type": "object",
                    "properties": {
                        "expression": {
                            "type": "string",
                            "description": "Math expression e.g. '2+2' or 'sqrt(144)'"
                        }
                    },
                    "required": ["expression"]
                }
            }
        },
        {
            "type": "function",
            "function": {
                "name": "get_weather",
                "description": "Get weather for a city",
                "parameters": {
                    "type": "object",
                    "properties": {
                        "city":  {"type": "string"},
                        "units": {"type": "string",
                                  "enum": ["celsius","fahrenheit"],
                                  "default": "celsius"}
                    },
                    "required": ["city"]
                }
            }
        }
    ]

    # Tool execution functions
    def execute_tool(name: str, args: dict) -> str:
        if name == "calculator":
            try:
                allowed = {k: v for k, v in math.__dict__.items()
                           if not k.startswith("_")}
                result  = eval(args["expression"],{"__builtins__":{}}, allowed)
                return json.dumps({"result": result, "expression": args["expression"]})
            except Exception as e:
                return json.dumps({"error": str(e)})

        elif name == "get_weather":
            # Simulated weather data
            weather_db = {
                "london": {"temp": 12, "condition": "cloudy",  "humidity": 80},
                "tokyo":  {"temp": 22, "condition": "sunny",   "humidity": 60},
                "paris":  {"temp": 15, "condition": "rainy",   "humidity": 85},
                "dubai":  {"temp": 38, "condition": "hot",     "humidity": 40},
            }
            city = args["city"].lower()
            data = weather_db.get(city, {"temp": 20, "condition": "unknown"})
            if args.get("units") == "fahrenheit":
                data["temp"] = data["temp"] * 9/5 + 32
                data["units"] = "°F"
            else:
                data["units"] = "°C"
            return json.dumps({**data, "city": args["city"]})

        return json.dumps({"error": f"Unknown tool: {name}"})

    # Agentic loop
    def agent_loop(user_query: str) -> str:
        print(f"\n  👤 User: {user_query}")
        messages = [{"role": "user", "content": user_query}]

        while True:
            response = client.chat.completions.create(
                model    = MODEL,
                messages = messages,
                tools    = tools,
                tool_choice = "auto",
                temperature = 0.0,
            )
            msg = response.choices[0].message

            # No tool call → final answer
            if not msg.tool_calls:
                print(f"  🤖 Agent: {msg.content}")
                return msg.content

            # Execute each tool call
            messages.append({"role": "assistant",
                              "content":    msg.content,
                              "tool_calls": [
                                  {"id": tc.id,
                                   "type": "function",
                                   "function": {"name": tc.function.name,
                                                "arguments": tc.function.arguments}}
                                  for tc in msg.tool_calls
                              ]})

            for tc in msg.tool_calls:
                args   = json.loads(tc.function.arguments)
                result = execute_tool(tc.function.name, args)
                print(f"  🔧 Tool [{tc.function.name}]: {args} → {result}")
                messages.append({
                    "role":         "tool",
                    "tool_call_id": tc.id,
                    "content":      result,
                })

    # Test queries
    queries = [
        "What is sqrt(256) + 100?",
        "What's the weather in Tokyo in Fahrenheit?",
        "Calculate compound interest: $10000 at 5% for 10 years (A = P*(1+r)^t)",
        "What's the weather in London and Paris? Which is warmer?",
    ]

    for q in queries:
        agent_loop(q)

# ════════════════════════════════════════════════════
# 2. STRUCTURED OUTPUT (JSON MODE)
# ════════════════════════════════════════════════════

def demo_structured_output():
    print("\n" + "="*55)
    print("📐 2. STRUCTURED OUTPUT DEMO")
    print("="*55)

    from pydantic import BaseModel, Field
    from typing   import Optional

    class PersonInfo(BaseModel):
        name:        str
        age:         Optional[int] = None
        occupation:  str
        skills:      list[str]
        summary:     str

    def extract_person_info(text: str) -> PersonInfo:
        response = client.chat.completions.create(
            model    = MODEL,
            messages = [
                {"role": "system",
                 "content": f"Extract person information. Return JSON matching: {PersonInfo.schema()}"},
                {"role": "user", "content": text},
            ],
            response_format = {"type": "json_object"},
            temperature     = 0.0,
        )
        data = json.loads(response.choices[0].message.content)
        return PersonInfo(**data)

    texts = [
        "Alice is a 32-year-old senior ML engineer at Google. She specializes in Python, TensorFlow, and distributed training.",
        "Bob has been working as a DevOps consultant for 8 years. He knows Docker, Kubernetes, Terraform, and AWS.",
    ]

    for text in texts:
        info = extract_person_info(text)
        print(f"\n  Input:  {text[:60]}...")
        print(f"  Name:   {info.name}")
        print(f"  Job:    {info.occupation}")
        print(f"  Skills: {info.skills}")

# ════════════════════════════════════════════════════
# 3. EMBEDDINGS & SIMILARITY SEARCH
# ════════════════════════════════════════════════════

def demo_embeddings():
    print("\n" + "="*55)
    print("🔢 3. EMBEDDINGS & SIMILARITY SEARCH DEMO")
    print("="*55)

    def embed(texts: list[str]) -> list[list[float]]:
        r = client.embeddings.create(
            input=[t.replace("\n"," ") for t in texts],
            model=EMBED_MODEL,
        )
        return [item.embedding for item in r.data]

    def cosine_similarity(a: list[float], b: list[float]) -> float:
        va = np.array(a, dtype=np.float32)
        vb = np.array(b, dtype=np.float32)
        return float(np.dot(va,vb) / (np.linalg.norm(va)*np.linalg.norm(vb)+1e-10))

    # Knowledge base
    docs = [
        "LangGraph builds stateful multi-agent workflows",
        "FastMCP makes building MCP servers easy with Python",
        "A2A protocol enables agent-to-agent communication",
        "RAG combines retrieval with language model generation",
        "Transformers use self-attention mechanisms",
        "Python is a general-purpose programming language",
        "Docker containers package applications and dependencies",
    ]
    doc_embeddings = embed(docs)

    # Search
    queries = [
        "How do agents communicate with each other?",
        "What is retrieval augmented generation?",
        "How do I build stateful agent workflows?",
    ]

    for query in queries:
        q_emb     = embed([query])[0]
        scores    = [(doc, cosine_similarity(q_emb, d_emb))
                     for doc, d_emb in zip(docs, doc_embeddings)]
        scores.sort(key=lambda x: x[1], reverse=True)

        print(f"\n  🔍 Query: '{query}'")
        for doc, score in scores[:3]:
            bar = "█" * int(score*20) + "░" * (20-int(score*20))
            print(f"     [{bar}] {score:.3f}  {doc}")

if __name__ == "__main__":
    demo_function_calling()
    demo_structured_output()
    demo_embeddings()
```

sections.title: What Are Agent Architectures?
sections.body:
> **"How agents are organized and how they collaborate"**

The structural patterns for organizing one or more agents to solve complex tasks. Just like software architecture patterns (MVC, microservices), agent architectures define who does what, how they communicate, and who's in charge.

sections.title: Architecture Patterns
sections.body:
```
┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│              ALL AGENT ARCHITECTURE PATTERNS                    │
└─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘

  1. SINGLE AGENT (ReAct Loop)
  ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
  One LLM + tools. Solves tasks step by step.

  User → [Agent] → Tool → [Agent] → Tool → [Agent] → Answer

  ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
  2. SUPERVISOR PATTERN
  ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
  One boss agent delegates to worker agents.

                  [SUPERVISOR]
                  /     |     \
           [Worker1] [Worker2] [Worker3]
           Research   Code      Write

  ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
  3. ROUTER PATTERN
  ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
  Routes tasks to the most suitable specialized agent.

  User Query → [ROUTER] → Classify → Send to correct agent
                               ├─ Math query   → MathAgent
                               ├─ Code query   → CodeAgent
                               └─ Search query → ResearchAgent

  ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
  4. PIPELINE PATTERN (Sequential)
  ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
  Each agent processes and passes output to next.

  [Agent1:Search] → [Agent2:Summarize] → [Agent3:Format] → Output

  ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
  5. DEBATE PATTERN
  ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
  Multiple agents argue for best answer, judge decides.

  [Agent A: "Answer is X"] ──┐
  [Agent B: "Answer is Y"] ──┤→ [JUDGE] → Best Answer
  [Agent C: "Answer is Z"] ──┘

  ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
  6. REFLECTION PATTERN
  ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
  Agent generates → Critic reviews → Agent improves.

  [Generator] → Output → [Critic] → Feedback → [Generator]
                    └──────── loop until good ──────────┘

  ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
  7. MIXTURE OF AGENTS (MoA)
  ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
  Multiple agents generate in parallel, aggregator combines.

  ┌── [Agent1:GPT4]   ──┐
  ├── [Agent2:Claude] ──┤→ [AGGREGATOR] → Combined Best Answer
  └── [Agent3:Gemini] ──┘

  ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
  8. HIERARCHICAL PATTERN
  ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
  Multi-level tree of agents with delegation.

         [CEO Agent]
         /          \
  [Manager A]    [Manager B]
   /      \         /      \
[Dev1] [Dev2]  [Test1]  [Test2]
```

sections.title: Layer 3 Code Examples
sections.body:
**What this code covers**

- Layer 3: All Agent Architecture Patterns Single Agent → Supervisor → Router → Pipeline → Reflection → MoA
- Simple single agent with ReAct loop.
- You are a supervisor.
- Classify this query.
- PATTERN 1: SINGLE AGENT (ReAct Loop)
- Improve based on feedback
- PATTERN 5: MIXTURE OF AGENTS (MoA)
- All agents respond in PARALLEL

**Defines:** `single_agent_demo()`, `call_llm()`, `supervisor_pattern()`, `router_pattern()`, `reflection_pattern()`, `mixture_of_agents()`, `SupervisorState`, `build_langgraph_supervisor()`

```python name=layer3_architectures/all_patterns.py
"""
Layer 3: All Agent Architecture Patterns
Single Agent → Supervisor → Router → Pipeline → Reflection → MoA
"""
import os
import json
import asyncio
from typing   import Literal
from dotenv   import load_dotenv
from openai   import AzureOpenAI
from langchain_openai  import AzureChatOpenAI
from langchain_core.messages import HumanMessage, SystemMessage, AIMessage
from langgraph.graph   import StateGraph, START, END
from typing            import TypedDict, Annotated
from langgraph.graph.message import add_messages

load_dotenv()

client = AzureOpenAI(
    azure_endpoint = os.getenv("AZURE_OPENAI_ENDPOINT"),
    api_key        = os.getenv("AZURE_OPENAI_API_KEY"),
    api_version    = os.getenv("AZURE_OPENAI_API_VERSION"),
)
MODEL = os.getenv("AZURE_OPENAI_DEPLOYMENT")

llm = AzureChatOpenAI(
    azure_endpoint   = os.getenv("AZURE_OPENAI_ENDPOINT"),
    api_key          = os.getenv("AZURE_OPENAI_API_KEY"),
    api_version      = os.getenv("AZURE_OPENAI_API_VERSION"),
    azure_deployment = MODEL,
    temperature      = 0.0,
)

# ════════════════════════════════════════════════════
# PATTERN 1: SINGLE AGENT (ReAct Loop)
# ════════════════════════════════════════════════════

def single_agent_demo(task: str) -> str:
    """Simple single agent with ReAct loop."""
    print(f"\n{'─'*55}")
    print(f"1️⃣  SINGLE AGENT: {task[:50]}")
    print(f"{'─'*55}")

    tools_schema = [
        {"type":"function","function":{
            "name":"search","description":"Search for info",
            "parameters":{"type":"object",
                          "properties":{"query":{"type":"string"}},
                          "required":["query"]}}},
        {"type":"function","function":{
            "name":"calculator","description":"Do math",
            "parameters":{"type":"object",
                          "properties":{"expr":{"type":"string"}},
                          "required":["expr"]}}},
    ]

    def run_tool(name, args):
        if name == "search":
            import math
            knowledge = {
                "python":    "Python 3.12 is the latest version (2024)",
                "langchain": "LangChain 0.3 supports LCEL, agents, and RAG",
                "mcp":       "MCP by Anthropic connects LLMs to tools",
            }
            q = args["query"].lower()
            for k, v in knowledge.items():
                if k in q:
                    return v
            return f"Information about: {args['query']}"
        elif name == "calculator":
            import math
            allowed = {k:v for k,v in math.__dict__.items() if not k.startswith("_")}
            return str(eval(args["expr"],{"__builtins__":{}}, allowed))

    messages = [{"role":"user","content":task}]
    steps    = 0

    while steps < 5:
        r   = client.chat.completions.create(
            model=MODEL, messages=messages,
            tools=tools_schema, tool_choice="auto",
            temperature=0.0,
        )
        msg = r.choices[0].message
        steps += 1

        if not msg.tool_calls:
            print(f"  ✅ Final: {msg.content}")
            return msg.content

        messages.append({
            "role":"assistant","content": msg.content or "",
            "tool_calls":[{
                "id":tc.id,"type":"function",
                "function":{"name":tc.function.name,
                            "arguments":tc.function.arguments}
            } for tc in msg.tool_calls]
        })

        for tc in msg.tool_calls:
            args   = json.loads(tc.function.arguments)
            result = run_tool(tc.function.name, args)
            print(f"  🔧 [{tc.function.name}] {args} → {result[:60]}")
            messages.append({"role":"tool",
                             "tool_call_id":tc.id,
                             "content":result})

    return "Max steps reached"

# ════════════════════════════════════════════════════
# PATTERN 2: SUPERVISOR
# ════════════════════════════════════════════════════

def call_llm(system: str, user: str, temperature: float = 0.0) -> str:
    r = client.chat.completions.create(
        model=MODEL, temperature=temperature,
        messages=[{"role":"system","content":system},
                  {"role":"user","content":user}],
        max_tokens=500,
    )
    return r.choices[0].message.content.strip()

def supervisor_pattern(task: str) -> str:
    print(f"\n{'─'*55}")
    print(f"2️⃣  SUPERVISOR PATTERN: {task[:50]}")
    print(f"{'─'*55}")

    # Workers
    def research_worker(subtask: str) -> str:
        return call_llm(
            "You are a research specialist. Find key facts.",
            subtask
        )

    def code_worker(subtask: str) -> str:
        return call_llm(
            "You are a Python expert. Write clean, typed code.",
            subtask
        )

    def writer_worker(subtask: str) -> str:
        return call_llm(
            "You are a technical writer. Write clear documentation.",
            subtask
        )

    workers = {
        "research": research_worker,
        "code":     code_worker,
        "write":    writer_worker,
    }

    # Supervisor plans
    plan_raw = call_llm(
        f"""You are a supervisor. Break this task into subtasks.
Return JSON: [{{"worker":"research|code|write","subtask":"..."}}]
Workers: {list(workers.keys())}""",
        f"Task: {task}"
    )

    try:
        import re
        match = re.search(r'\[.*\]', plan_raw, re.DOTALL)
        plan  = json.loads(match.group()) if match else []
    except:
        plan = [{"worker":"research","subtask":task}]

    results = {}
    for step in plan:
        worker  = step.get("worker","research")
        subtask = step.get("subtask", task)
        print(f"  📋 Delegating to [{worker}]: {subtask[:50]}")
        result  = workers.get(worker, research_worker)(subtask)
        results[worker] = result
        print(f"  ✅ [{worker}] done: {result[:60]}...")

    # Supervisor synthesizes
    combined = "\n".join([f"[{k}]: {v[:200]}" for k,v in results.items()])
    final    = call_llm(
        "You are a supervisor. Synthesize worker results into one answer.",
        f"Task: {task}\nWorker Results:\n{combined}"
    )
    print(f"\n  🎯 Synthesis: {final[:100]}...")
    return final

# ════════════════════════════════════════════════════
# PATTERN 3: ROUTER
# ════════════════════════════════════════════════════

def router_pattern(query: str) -> str:
    print(f"\n{'─'*55}")
    print(f"3️⃣  ROUTER PATTERN: {query[:50]}")
    print(f"{'─'*55}")

    # Route classifier
    route_raw = call_llm(
        """Classify this query. Return JSON ONLY:
{"route": "math|code|research|general", "reason": "..."}""",
        query
    )
    try:
        import re
        match = re.search(r'\{.*\}', route_raw, re.DOTALL)
        route_info = json.loads(match.group()) if match else {"route":"general"}
    except:
        route_info = {"route":"general"}

    route = route_info.get("route","general")
    print(f"  🔀 Routed to: [{route}] — {route_info.get('reason','')[:60]}")

    # Specialized agents
    if route == "math":
        return call_llm("You are a math expert. Solve step by step.", query)
    elif route == "code":
        return call_llm("You are a Python expert. Write clean code with type hints.", query)
    elif route == "research":
        return call_llm("You are a researcher. Provide comprehensive findings.", query)
    else:
        return call_llm("You are a helpful assistant.", query)

# ════════════════════════════════════════════════════
# PATTERN 4: REFLECTION
# ════════════════════════════════════════════════════

def reflection_pattern(task: str, max_rounds: int = 3) -> str:
    print(f"\n{'─'*55}")
    print(f"4️⃣  REFLECTION PATTERN: {task[:50]}")
    print(f"{'─'*55}")

    # Generate initial response
    output = call_llm(
        "You are an expert. Produce your best work.",
        task,
        temperature=0.3
    )
    print(f"  ✏️  Draft 1: {output[:80]}...")

    for round_n in range(1, max_rounds + 1):
        # Critic evaluates
        critique = call_llm(
            """You are a strict critic. Evaluate this output.
Return JSON: {"score": 1-10, "approved": true/false, "feedback": "..."}""",
            f"Task: {task}\nOutput: {output}"
        )
        try:
            import re
            match    = re.search(r'\{.*\}', critique, re.DOTALL)
            crit_obj = json.loads(match.group()) if match else {"score":7,"approved":True}
        except:
            crit_obj = {"score":7,"approved":True}

        score    = crit_obj.get("score",7)
        approved = crit_obj.get("approved",True)
        feedback = crit_obj.get("feedback","")

        print(f"  🔍 Critique round {round_n}: score={score}/10 | {feedback[:60]}")

        if approved or score >= 8:
            print(f"  ✅ Approved after {round_n} round(s)!")
            break

        # Improve based on feedback
        output = call_llm(
            "You are an expert. Improve your output based on critique.",
            f"Original task: {task}\nPrevious output: {output}\nCritique: {feedback}\nImprove it.",
            temperature=0.2
        )
        print(f"  ✏️  Improved draft {round_n+1}: {output[:80]}...")

    return output

# ════════════════════════════════════════════════════
# PATTERN 5: MIXTURE OF AGENTS (MoA)
# ════════════════════════════════════════════════════

async def mixture_of_agents(question: str) -> str:
    print(f"\n{'─'*55}")
    print(f"5️⃣  MIXTURE OF AGENTS: {question[:50]}")
    print(f"{'─'*55}")

    personas = [
        ("Technical Expert",   "Answer technically with precision and detail."),
        ("Simple Explainer",   "Explain simply for a beginner, use analogies."),
        ("Critical Thinker",   "Challenge assumptions, consider edge cases."),
    ]

    async def get_response(persona: str, instruction: str) -> str:
        r = await asyncio.get_event_loop().run_in_executor(
            None, lambda: call_llm(
                f"You are a {persona}. {instruction}", question
            )
        )
        return r

    # All agents respond in PARALLEL
    tasks   = [get_response(p, i) for p, i in personas]
    answers = await asyncio.gather(*tasks)

    for (persona, _), answer in zip(personas, answers):
        print(f"  🤖 [{persona}]: {answer[:80]}...")

    # Aggregator combines the best elements
    combined = "\n\n".join([
        f"[{p}]: {a}"
        for (p, _), a in zip(personas, answers)
    ])
    final = call_llm(
        "Synthesize these expert perspectives into the best possible answer.",
        f"Question: {question}\n\nPerspectives:\n{combined}"
    )
    print(f"\n  🏆 Combined: {final[:120]}...")
    return final

# ════════════════════════════════════════════════════
# LANGGRAPH SUPERVISOR (Production-grade)
# ════════════════════════════════════════════════════

class SupervisorState(TypedDict):
    messages: Annotated[list, add_messages]
    next:     str
    results:  dict

def build_langgraph_supervisor():
    """LangGraph supervisor with conditional routing."""

    def supervisor_node(state: SupervisorState) -> dict:
        last_msg = state["messages"][-1].content
        r = llm.invoke([
            SystemMessage(content="""You control worker agents.
Choose next worker or FINISH.
Return JSON: {"next": "researcher|coder|writer|FINISH", "reason": "..."}"""),
            HumanMessage(content=f"Task: {last_msg}\nResults so far: {state.get('results',{})}")
        ])
        try:
            import re
            match = re.search(r'\{.*\}', r.content, re.DOTALL)
            data  = json.loads(match.group()) if match else {"next":"FINISH"}
        except:
            data  = {"next":"FINISH"}
        print(f"  🎭 Supervisor → {data['next']}")
        return {"next": data["next"]}

    def researcher_node(state: SupervisorState) -> dict:
        last = state["messages"][-1].content
        r    = llm.invoke([SystemMessage(content="You are a researcher."),
                           HumanMessage(content=last)])
        results = {**state.get("results",{}), "research": r.content[:200]}
        print(f"  🔬 Researcher done")
        return {"results": results, "messages": [AIMessage(content=r.content)]}

    def coder_node(state: SupervisorState) -> dict:
        last = state["messages"][-1].content
        r    = llm.invoke([SystemMessage(content="You are a Python expert."),
                           HumanMessage(content=last)])
        results = {**state.get("results",{}), "code": r.content[:200]}
        print(f"  💻 Coder done")
        return {"results": results, "messages": [AIMessage(content=r.content)]}

    def writer_node(state: SupervisorState) -> dict:
        last    = state["messages"][-1].content
        context = json.dumps(state.get("results",{}))
        r       = llm.invoke([SystemMessage(content="You are a writer."),
                              HumanMessage(content=f"Write final answer for: {last}\nContext: {context}")])
        print(f"  ✍️  Writer done")
        return {"results": {**state.get("results",{}), "final": r.content},
                "messages": [AIMessage(content=r.content)]}

    def route(state: SupervisorState) -> Literal["researcher","coder","writer","__end__"]:
        nxt = state.get("next","FINISH")
        if nxt == "FINISH": return "__end__"
        return nxt.lower().replace("er","er")   # researcher, coder, writer

    g = StateGraph(SupervisorState)
    g.add_node("supervisor",  supervisor_node)
    g.add_node("researcher",  researcher_node)
    g.add_node("coder",       coder_node)
    g.add_node("writer",      writer_node)

    g.add_edge(START, "supervisor")
    g.add_conditional_edges("supervisor", route,
                             {"researcher":"researcher",
                              "coder":"coder",
                              "writer":"writer",
                              "__end__":END})
    g.add_edge("researcher", "supervisor")
    g.add_edge("coder",      "supervisor")
    g.add_edge("writer",     "supervisor")

    return g.compile()

if __name__ == "__main__":
    # Run all patterns
    single_agent_demo("What is LangChain and calculate 15% of 2500?")
    supervisor_pattern("Research Python async patterns and write a code example")
    router_pattern("Calculate the area of a circle with radius 7")
    router_pattern("Write a Python class for a binary search tree")
    reflection_pattern("Explain the difference between RAG and fine-tuning")

    asyncio.run(mixture_of_agents(
        "What is the best approach for building production AI agents?"
    ))

    # LangGraph supervisor
    print("\n6️⃣  LANGGRAPH SUPERVISOR")
    graph  = build_langgraph_supervisor()
    result = graph.invoke({
        "messages": [HumanMessage(content="Research RAG and write a Python example")],
        "next":     "",
        "results":  {},
    })
    print(f"\n  ✅ Final: {result['results'].get('final','')[:200]}...")
```

sections.body:
> **"Agents are only as powerful as their tools"**

Tools are functions an agent can call to interact with the world — search the web, run code, query databases, send emails. The tool ecosystem is what transforms an LLM from a text predictor into an autonomous agent.
